issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s successor to the reversion in part of premises let under a single tenancy may exercise landlord rights over that part without the tenant’s consent when the reversion has been severed and the applicable rule recognizes that right.
material_facts: The tenant occupied two adjacent shops under one lease from two co-owners.
The appellant acquired one co-owner’s interest, and a later partition allotted one shop exclusively to the appellant.
The appellant sought eviction from that shop on a bona fide need ground, which the statutory authorities found established.
The High Court set aside the eviction order on the basis that the tenancy could not be split without the tenant’s consent.
An earlier decision of the same High Court had held that the landlord-successor rule applied to partition.
issues.conclusion: The restriction against splitting a tenancy did not bar the appellant from seeking possession of the shop allotted to him. The tenant’s consent was not required, and the eviction order was restored. The Court applied the earlier High Court rule to this case without deciding whether that rule was correct.
issues.legal_principle: Section 109 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 provides an exception to the general rule that a landlord cannot split the unity and integrity of a tenancy: an assignee of part of the reversion may exercise the lessor’s rights over the part assigned, without consensual attornment or the tenant’s consent. The Court relied on Kannyan v. Alikutty, AIR 1920 Mad 838 (FB), distinguished Badri Narain Jha v. Rameshwar Dayal Singh, [1951] SCR 153 as concerning division among lessees rather than severance of the reversion, and applied Ram Chandra Singh v. Ram Saran, AIR 1978 All 173, which treated partition as within the rule. The Court did not pronounce on the correctness of that decision.

predicates.eviction_proceeding: A landlord seeks possession from a tenant through an eviction proceeding.
predicates.tenancy_created_by_single_lease: The tenant holds the relevant premises under one lease rather than separate leases for each part.
predicates.claimant_became_exclusive_owner_of_part_: The claimant became the exclusive owner of a portion of the premises previously let as part of the tenancy.
predicates.reversion_severance_rule_applies_to_the_: The applicable rule treats the claimant’s acquisition as severing the reversion and recognizes the claimant’s rights over the acquired portion.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding concerns premises held under one lease and the claimant becomes the exclusive owner of a part under a rule recognizing severance of the reversion, the claimant may seek possession of that part without the tenant’s consent.

issues.legal_issue: A judge of a High Court must follow an earlier decision of that same court on the point, or refer the matter to a larger bench if the judge disagrees, unless a larger-bench ruling has displaced it.
material_facts: The tenant challenged the eviction order in a writ petition before the High Court.
An earlier decision of that High Court had held that the landlord-successor rule applied to partition.
The Court stated that the judge deciding the later matter should have followed that earlier decision unless a larger bench had ruled otherwise, or referred the disagreement to a Division Bench.
issues.conclusion: The High Court judge should have followed the earlier decision of the same High Court or, if differing from it, referred the matter to a Division Bench.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on Ram Chandra Singh v. Ram Saran, AIR 1978 All 173, and the rule of precedent within the same High Court: a judge should follow the earlier decision unless a larger bench has ruled contrary to it; a judge who disagrees should have the matter considered by a Division Bench.

predicates.single_judge_writ_review: A single judge reviews the matter in a writ proceeding.
predicates.earlier_same_high_court_decision_on_the_: The same High Court had already decided the legal point in an earlier case.
predicates.no_contrary_larger_bench_decision: No decision of a larger bench of that High Court had displaced the earlier ruling.

issues.definition: When a single judge reviews a matter and an earlier decision of the same High Court governs the point without contrary larger-bench authority, the judge must follow it or refer a disagreement to a larger bench.
